record.original_question: Let (W1,S1) and (W2,S2) be Coxeter systems, let J1 subseteq S1 and J2 subseteq S2, let u,v in W1^{J1} and w,z in W2^{J2}, and let f : [u,v] -> [w,z] be a poset isomorphism such that f([u,v]^{J1}) = [w,z]^{J2}. Must the parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials satisfy P_{u,v}^{J1,q}(q) = P_{w,z}^{J2,q}(q)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.6. Let (W1,S1), (W2,S2) be two Coxeter systems, J1 subseteq S1, J2 subseteq S2, u,v in W1^{J1}, w,z in W2^{J2} and f : [u,v] -> [w,z] be a poset isomorphism such that f([u,v]^{J1}) = [w,z]^{J2}. Then P_{u,v}^{J1,q}(q) = P_{w,z}^{J2,q}(q).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(W_1,S_1)$ and $(W_2,S_2)$ be Coxeter systems, equipped with their (strong) Bruhat orders. For $i=1,2$, let $J_i \subseteq S_i$, and let $W_i^{J_i}$ denote the set of minimal-length coset representatives of $W_i / W_{J_i}$ (where $W_{J_i}$ is the parabolic subgroup generated by $J_i$). For $u,v \in W_1^{J_1}$ with $u\le v$ and $w,z \in W_2^{J_2}$ with $w\le z$, write $[u,v]=\{x\in W_1 : u\le x\le v\}$ for the Bruhat interval, and $[u,v]^{J_1} := [u,v]\cap W_1^{J_1}$; similarly $[w,z]^{J_2}$.

For a Coxeter system $(W,S)$, $J\subseteq S$, and $u\le v$ with $u,v\in W^J$, let $P_{u,v}^{J,q}(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q]$ denote the parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial of type $q$ (Deodhar's parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial corresponding to the parameter $q$).

Suppose $f:[u,v]\to[w,z]$ is an isomorphism of posets (with respect to Bruhat order) such that $f([u,v]^{J_1}) = [w,z]^{J_2}$. Must one have
$$P_{u,v}^{J_1,q}(q) \;=\; P_{w,z}^{J_2,q}(q)?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is a refined parabolic combinatorial invariance statement; recent work proves it in special cases (e.g., lower Bruhat intervals) and shows equivalence with Lusztig–Dyer's classical conjecture and Marietti's parabolic version, but the full conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: On combinatorial invariance of parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Proves new cases of the parabolic combinatorial invariance conjecture; full conjecture not established.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture remains open in general; partial cases proved.

status_evidence.title: Equivalence between invariance conjectures for parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Shows the classical Lusztig–Dyer conjecture, Marietti's parabolic conjecture, and a refined parabolic version are equivalent.
status_evidence.claim: All three forms equivalent, hence open jointly.

status_evidence.title: The combinatorial invariance conjecture for parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of lower intervals
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the parabolic conjecture for lower Bruhat intervals.
